latest.question: Deputy Naoise Ó Muirí asked the Minister for Agriculture, Food and the Marine if he will outline the framework set out under the National Bioeconomy Strategy 2026–2030.
latest.reply:
At the outset, I wish to highlight that the new National Bioeconomy Strategy 2026-2030 has not yet been published. This will occur on the occasion of the Global Bioeconomy Summit which the Government, in conjunction with the International Advisory Council for the Global Bioeconomy, will host here in Dublin on October 20th and 21st. The Taoiseach, Minister O'Brien and I look forward to presenting the Strategy to the national and international audience that will gather for that important Summit.
Notwithstanding this, I can refer the Deputy to the framework of the Strategy that was set out in the draft that was issued for public consultation in July. The Strategy’s Vision is that by 2030, Ireland’s bioeconomy is a core driver of economic prosperity, climate action, and rural regeneration. It is characterised by the sustainable and circular use of biological resources, innovative high-value industries, and thriving local communities.
The Strategy focuses on five strategic objectives and contains targeted actions for each of these. They are:
• Scaling Infrastructure, Technology and Investment.
• Strengthening Market Demand and Development.
• Leveraging Innovation, Knowledge and Skills.
• Bioeconomy as a tool for Climate Action and Circularity.
• Improving Governance, Cooperation and Partnerships.
The Strategy also provides for focused development across five priority sectors where Ireland has strong potential to expand sustainable biobased activity. They include the Agri-Bioeconom

latest.question: Deputy Shónagh Ní Raghallaigh asked the Minister for Agriculture, Food and the Marine if he will consider adding a cap on the number of breeding females permitted within a dog breeding establishment to the legislation proposed in this area.
latest.reply:
In order to bring a coherent approach to dog control, policy and legislative responsibility under both the Control of Dogs Act 1986 and the Dog Breeding Establishments Act 2010 transferred to my Department last year. In both cases, local authorities retain responsibility for all operational and enforcement matters.
On 19th May 2026, my Department published draft legislation, the Dog Breeding Establishments Bill 2026 to update the existing regulatory framework for dog breeding establishments in Ireland across three key areas - welfare and breeding, sales and record keeping, and administration and enforcement.
The Bill was approved for priority drafting and is currently undergoing pre-legislative scrutiny with the Oireachtas Joint Committee on Agriculture.
The Bill has seventeen Heads and addresses three broad areas: welfare and breeding standards, sales and record-keeping, and administration and enforcement.
It seeks to address concerns about excessive numbers through a mandatory staffing ratio of 1:20 which creates an indirect but real constraint on establishment size. The strengthened improvement notice regime will explicitly empower authorised persons to require a reduction in the number of dogs on premises where welfare concerns arise.
Local authorities also retain the ability to set conditions on the number of breeding females as part of the registration process, and this avenue remains open to them, particularly in respect of new applications.

latest.question: Deputy Darren O'Rourke asked the Minister for Agriculture, Food and the Marine when the updated Land Use Strategy will be published; and to provide an update on same.
latest.reply:
The Land Use Review Phase 2 titled “A Living Land” was published in July of this year. It provides an evidence base to inform and support landholders and policymakers in their future decisions for land-use, in the context of achieving Ireland’s agricultural, socio-economic, climate and environmental objectives.
The report is not an articulation of government policy or a strategy in relation to land use, given that there are many economic, environmental, and social elements to be balanced in considering land use. Rather, this report will help to inform and support future considerations in this complex area. For example, the role of State-owned lands in leading the way to achieve integrated land use objectives.
To consider fully the recommendations of the Phase 2 of the Land Use Review, my Department has committed to co-chair with DCEE, a Land Use Taskforce, with members to include DHLGH and other relevant Departments and bodies.
Establishment of a Land Use Taskforce is the next step to examine how the State can encourage optimal use of land to meet a variety of societal needs including socio-economic, restoring nature, improving water quality, enhancing climate adaptation and mitigation.

latest.question: Deputy Aindrias Moynihan asked the Minister for Agriculture, Food and the Marine the number and value of TAMS solar applications approved and not approved to date in 2026; if he will approve additional funding to meet the demand.
latest.reply:
The Targeted Agriculture Modernisation Scheme (TAMS) is a demand-led scheme with a defined budgetary allocation. The budgetary allocation for TAMS 3 is spread across all eleven sub schemes therefore it is not possible to allocate a budget to each of the eleven schemes individually.
TAMS 3 has been hugely successful to date, with over €195 million issuing to farmers since payments commenced in June 2024. Over the first eight tranches of the scheme, all valid applications received were approved.
However, to ensure the available budget for TAMS 3 is distributed fairly over the remainder of the current CAP programming period, it was necessary to limit the number of approved applications per tranche from Tranche 9 onwards by applying ranking and selection criteria to manage the budget to the end of 2027.
Specifically in respect of the Solar Capital Investment Scheme (SCIS) the number of applications and the level of funding provided to date has also well exceeded expectations, to the extent that more than 20% of the TAMS budget is being spent on SCIS.
A total of 7,331 applications have been received under the SCIS with approvals of 3,787 issuing to farmers allowing them to proceed with their investments. The average payment under SCIS is €18,777 per application with an estimated value of the overall approved applications in excess of €71m. Payments amounting to €39.5m have issued to 2,107 farmers since payments commenced in June 2024.

latest.question: Deputy Pádraig Mac Lochlainn asked the Minister for Agriculture, Food and the Marine when he will publish the report from the Food Vision Seafood Sector Group (details supplied).
latest.reply:
In February this year, Minister Heydon and I established a working group under the auspices of Food Vision 2030 - the Food Vision Seafood Sector Group - to consider the challenges facing all three components of the Irish seafood sector (catch fisheries, aquaculture and seafood processing).
The Group’s overarching objective was to identify and develop a framework of measures to respond to these current challenges. I engaged Mr. Michael Berkery to Chair the Group and to submit an independent report to me by June 2026.
I am currently considering Mr. Berkery's report and will make a decision on its publication in due course.

latest.question: Deputy Jennifer Whitmore asked the Minister for Agriculture, Food and the Marine when the Dog Control Stakeholder Group Report will be published.
latest.reply:
I have recently received the report of the Dog Control Stakeholder Group which was established in 2024, which I am considering, including any recommendations in relation to dog control legislation.
My Department is considering avenues of implementation, in particular the forthcoming Animal Welfare Strategy, scheduled for publication in the near term. I also hope to publish the Dog Control Stakeholder Group report shortly.
The insights and recommendations arising from the Group’s work will make an important contribution to the ongoing development of policy in relation to dog control, responsible dog ownership, public safety and animal welfare.
I am deeply grateful for the time and effort devoted by the group to this important area of public policy.

latest.question: Deputy Keira Keogh asked the Minister for Agriculture, Food and the Marine the urgent measures he and his Department is taking to address the backlog in aquaculture licence renewals, reviews and new applications in County Mayo; whether additional resources or personnel will be allocated to the Aquaculture and Foreshore Management Division to tackle the significant backlog, in view of the fact that some licences have expired and some applications submitted remain undetermined due to delays.
latest.reply:
Applications for aquaculture and foreshore licences are considered by my Department in accordance with the provisions of the Fisheries (Amendment) Act 1997, the Foreshore Act 1933 (as amended) and applicable national and EU legislation. The licensing process is complex and involves consultation with a wide range of scientific and technical advisors, in addition to various Statutory Consultees. The legislation also provides for a period of public consultation.
The length of time taken to process an aquaculture licence application varies depending on a number of factors including location, species, scale and intensity of production, statutory status of sites and potential visual impact. My Department also takes full account of all scientific and technical advice, in addition to all issues identified during the public and statutory consultation phases.
Further factors that can impact the time taken to process an application can include; the requirement for an Appropriate Assessment and whether the application is required to be accompanied by an Environmental Impact Assessment Report; the need for additional underwater or archaeological assessments, etc. Decisions in respect of aquaculture licence applications are only taken following the fullest consideration of all consultations and public interest elements of each application, including environmental considerations.

latest.question: Deputy John Clendennen asked the Minister for Agriculture, Food and the Marine the measures he is taking to enable farmers to participate directly in Ireland's renewable energy transition; and the opportunity he foresees for renewable energy to provide an income stream for farms.
latest.reply:
As the Deputy will be aware overall national energy policy formation is the direct responsibility of my colleague the Minister for Climate Energy and the Environment. My Department works closely with the Department of Climate Energy and the Environment on energy related matters from an agricultural perspective, as well as with a wide range of industry and other stakeholder groups.
Solar and Biomethane are renewable energy options available to farmers which can improve their financial resilience through the diversification of their income stream. Both Solar and Biomethane have received significant support from my Department.
My Department co-led the development of the National Biomethane Strategy, with the Department of Climate Energy and the Environment, which was published in 2024. This was Ireland’s first major policy statement on Biomethane. A key outcome of the Strategy was the Biomethane Capital Grant Scheme, which was run by my Department. The scheme recently concluded with funding of approximately €19 million issued to 7 projects. Not only will these projects contribute to the achievement of Ireland’s Biomethane target set out in the Climate Action Plan, but they also represent an opportunity for farmers to provide feedstock for biomethane generation, thus providing a new income stream for farmers. latest.question: Deputy Paul Murphy asked the Minister for Agriculture, Food and the Marine if he will support a ban on surgical artificial insemination of greyhounds.
latest.reply:
The Veterinary Council of Ireland (VCI) in April 2024 updated its Code of Professional Conduct for Veterinary Practitioners to prohibit veterinarians from carrying out surgical artificial insemination in dogs due to ethical and welfare considerations. However, this new prohibition does not apply to greyhounds, as the practice is provided for in legislation under the Artificial Insemination of Greyhound Regulations 2005.
The report of the Working Group on Control of Dogs, which was approved by Government in March 2023, and has been published online at: www.gov.ie/en/publication/0d6d7-working-group-on-control-of-dogs/#report-of-the-working-group-on-the-control-of-dogs, includes a recommendation that surgical artificial insemination in canines be prohibited, where the word canine encompasses all breeds of dogs.
In 2024, my Department held a public consultation on whether the practice of carrying out surgical artificial insemination in greyhounds should be banned or not and the results of the public consultation are now available on: www.gov.ie/en/department-of-agriculture-food-and-the-marine/publications/animal-welfare/#surgical-artificial-insemination-in-greyhounds.
In compliance of section 5 of the Greyhound Racing Act, S.I. latest.question: Deputy Martin Kenny asked the Minister for Agriculture, Food and the Marine the supports his Department is providing to Irish farmers to deal with rising input costs in the agriculture sector.
latest.reply:
The agri-food sector has demonstrated its ongoing adaptability and resilience despite numerous uncertainties and economic pressure in recent years. The Government continues to provide strong support to farmers via Ireland’s €10.3 billion CAP Strategic Plan, as well as other national sectoral schemes. This results in payments to support farmers of over €2 billion annually.
I am conscious of the exceptional cost pressures family farms are facing at present. I introduced the Fuel Income Support Scheme as a targeted income support, alongside the fuel excise and levy reductions and delay of Carbon Tax increases introduced by Government. To date total payments of €26.52m have been made under the Fuel Income Support Scheme, with over 31,000 farmers and contractors paid.
I acknowledge that the impact of prolonged dry weather this year has increased the challenges family farmers face this year. The dry conditions resulted in significant supplementary feeding on affected farms and the use of silage and other fodder conserved for winter feeding. This has increased costs while also reducing the quantity of fodder available for the coming winter. Responding to the ongoing challenges, I have also availed of the flexibility to increase the rate of advance payments under the BISS, CRISS and Eco-scheme from 70% to 75%, helping to put more money in farmers pockets as early as possible in the year.
Flexibilities have also been provided on requirements associated with certain actions under the A

latest.question: Deputy Joe Neville asked the Minister for Agriculture, Food and the Marine the measures his Department has taken to introduce additional resources for enforcement of animal welfare legislation.
latest.reply:
My Department has lead policy responsibility within government for animal welfare, which is protected by legislation. I am committed to ensuring that animal welfare standards are vigorously applied in a fair and even-handed manner. All reports of alleged animal neglect or cruelty received by my Department are investigated and appropriate action is taken.
My Department and authorised officers appointed under the Animal Health and Welfare Act 2013, including An Garda Síochána, Customs agents, local authorities and the National Society for the Prevention of Cruelty to Animals (NSPCA), undertake appropriate enforcement action, where breaches or shortcomings are identified. Since the Act came into operation in March 2014, 230 cases have been successfully prosecuted by my Department and the NSPCA.
My Department has policy and legislative responsibility for the Control of Horses Act 1996. However, Local Authorities are responsible for operation of the Act, and they may take a range of actions in relation to equines, including prohibiting horses in certain areas, issuing licences and seizing horses. These powers can be used in respect of straying horses, including horses put on land without owner’s permission, including public land. Local authorities may also prosecute offenders.

latest.question: Deputy Barry Ward asked the Minister for Agriculture, Food and the Marine the position regarding work ongoing to address animal cruelty concerns related to the export of live animals; and if he has engaged with animal welfare organisations in this regard.
latest.reply:
The intra community trade and export of live animals to third countries is a private commercial activity which is regulated by my Department in accordance with EU and National Regulations. Relevant Regulations for this sector include Council Regulation (EC) No. 1/2005 on the protection of animals during transport and related operations which is given effect at national level by S.I. No. 675/2006 European Communities (Animal Transport and Control Post) Regulations 2006. S.I. No. 580/2007 - Diseases of Animals (Animal Transport) (Roll-on Roll-off Vessels) Order 2007 and S.I. No. 356/2016 - Carriage of Livestock by Sea Regulations 2016.
My Department demands the highest standards of animal welfare at every stage of the animal’s life, including during transport. My Department has continuously reinforced its practical, administrative and legislative measures to protect the welfare of animals during transport, often going beyond the minimum requirements of EU law, for example in terms of extra space for calves, more frequent driver retraining and temperature control.
Ireland is a major livestock trading country. Based on data collected by my Department, from 1 January to 20 September 2026, some 278,000 bovines were the subject of intra-community trade, or exports to third countries, from Ireland; 203,000 of these bovines were un-weaned calves. examples.question: Deputy Emer Currie asked the Minister for Education and Youth the position regarding a project (details supplied).
examples.reply:
As previously advised to the Deputy, the school referred to was approved to enter my Department's pipeline of projects under the Additional School Accommodation (ASA) scheme.
The project received approval from my Department to commence construction in January 2026. More recently, Department officials were notified by the school authorities that construction has now commenced. Expected completion to coincide with the start of the new school year.

examples.question: Deputy Paul Donnelly asked the Minister for Defence if she is aware of Irish Defence Forces members participating in military competitions with the Israeli Defence Forces; and if confirmed, her views on such on participation.
examples.reply:
The Defence Forces participate in international military competitions in order to promote in the Defence Forces the adoption of international best practice, exchange of tactics, techniques and procedures (TTP) and encourage the development of military skills. It also contributes to the development of particular military skillsets and doctrines.
The decision on who to invite to these competitions lies with the hosting nation. I am informed by the military authorities that the Defence Forces have not participated in any military competitions organised by the Israeli Defence Forces. I am also informed that, to date, no Defence Forces team has reported Israeli Defence Forces participation in competitions attended by Defence Forces personnel.

examples.question: Deputy Erin McGreehan asked the Minister for Agriculture, Food and the Marine for an update on the timeline and commencement dates for the basic income support for sustainability scheme.
examples.reply:
My Department is fully committed to making payments to farmers under the various schemes at the earliest date possible and to the maximum number of farmers possible. This commitment to farmers is evidenced in the very high payment rates achieved across all schemes over the last number of years in both EU and Exchequer funded schemes.
The timelines for all schemes, including the planned payment dates, have been set after extensive consultation with farmers and taking account of application systems, monitoring systems, validation and processing systems and payment systems.
In 2025, my Department commenced payments under the Basic Income Support for Sustainability (BISS) scheme from October 16th ensuring money flowed as soon as practically possible to farmers.
This payment date is in line with the traditional payment date of the BISS Scheme to farmers and is as outlined in the Farmers' Charter.

examples.question: Deputy Tom Brabazon asked the Minister for Housing, Local Government and Heritage for an update on the financial contribution scheme; and the rationale to no longer fund this scheme.
examples.reply:
The Government’s new housing plan, Delivering Homes, Building Communities 2025-2030, includes measures to increase delivery of housing for older people through increased delivery of social housing, increased delivery of more suitable homes in private housing and increased choice to support voluntary rightsizing, including a review of the operation of existing local authority financial contribution schemes.
I understand that existing financial contribution schemes in place in some local authorities are non-statutory and therefore a matter for the individual local authorities. Consideration will be given to a review of the operation of existing local authority financial contribution schemes and my Department is advancing these measures now incorporated in the new housing plan.

examples.question: Deputy Réada Cronin asked the Minister for Climate, Energy and the Environment what specific regulatory changes are being sought by Re-Turn for the proposed rPET reprocessing facility; the Department's position on the establishment of such a processing facility.
examples.reply:
Re-turn is a producer-led and owned, not-for-profit company established by beverage producers to meet their obligations under the Separate Collection (Deposit Return Scheme) Regulations.
Re-turn has stated its ambition to develop an rPET reprocessing facility in Ireland. In this regard, Re-turn has briefed me and Departmental officials on its plans.
The matter remains under consideration, with the Department considering the various public policy considerations that arise.

examples.question: Deputy John Paul O'Shea asked the Minister for Transport further to Parliamentary Question No.199 of 16 April 2026, regarding Ireland's current position (details supplied); whether he has articulated this position either internally with Irish officials or with European counterparts; if so, if he will provide details of what was articulated and through which medium.
examples.reply:
I am aware of the concerns raised by car rental fleet operators regarding the Clean Corporate Vehicles proposal. We engage regularly with representatives from this sector and have met with them several times over the past year, including discussions specifically on this proposal.
It should be noted that the measure remains at proposal stage, with negotiations currently underway at EU level. The Regulation will not be finalised until such time as an agreement is reached between the Council and the European Parliament. This process is expected to run through 2026, which intersects with Ireland’s Presidency of the Council of the EU.

examples.question: Deputy Paul Murphy asked the Minister for Agriculture, Food and the Marine the numerical, scientific and editorial verification carried out before the Wildlife Unit End of Year Report for 2025 that was approved for publication; whether further errors have since been identified; and whether his Department will publish an amended report clearly identifying all corrections.
examples.reply:
The Wildlife Report compiled by my Department has stated that there was 7,625 badger captures in the vaccine area in 2025. This is the correct figure. The figure of 8,123 is the number of badger captures that were recorded in vaccine areas for 2024. Table 4 in the report states the correct figures of badger captures for 2024 and 2025.
For the purposes of clarity the figure for 2024 will be removed from the body of the text.

examples.question: Deputy Carol Nolan asked the Minister for Social Protection the number of people who have had their receipt of jobseeker's allowance or jobseeker's benefit permanently withdrawn or revoked for breach of the conditions associated with their claim, and who have not subsequently had their claim reinstated, from January 2020 to date.
examples.reply:
To be eligible for a Jobseeker's payment a person must satisfy all the eligibility criteria for the relevant scheme.
Where a claim has been stopped, it will only be re-instated following an application by the customer and where all conditions of the scheme are satisfied.
It is not possible to provide data on the number of claims stopped and not subsequently re-instated due to the large churn on jobseekers schemes and the many legitimate reasons that claims are stopped.
I trust that this clarifies matters for the Deputy.

examples.question: Deputy Ruth Coppinger asked the Minister for Social Protection the annual figures since 2015 for appeals lodged with the social welfare appeals office querying a refusal based on the habitual residence condition, by Irish citizens and non-Irish nationals, in tabular form.
examples.reply:
I am advised by the Chief Appeals Officer that the Social Welfare Appeals Office does not collate data on appeals specifically relating to the Habitual Residence Condition, therefore the statistical information is not available.
I trust this clarifies the matter for the Deputy.

examples.question: Deputy John Paul O'Shea asked the Minister for Housing, Local Government and Heritage the number of appeals involving the rating of agricultural or horticultural buildings have been brought before the Valuation Tribunal since 2020; the number that were successful; and the average length of time taken to determine these appeals.
examples.reply:
As the Valuation Tribunal is independent in the performance of its functions, my Department does not hold the information requested in relation to the number of appeals involving the rating of agricultural or horticultural buildings have been brought before the Valuation Tribunal since 2020; the number that were successful; or the average length of time taken to determine these appeals.
It is noted that certain information on Valuation Tribunal appeals activity is included in the Tribunal's Annual Reports, available on the organisation's website at: www.valuationtribunal.ie/about-us/publications/.
Judgements of the Valuation Tribunal are also published and can be accessed on the Tribunal's website (at: www.valuationtribunal.ie/judgments/) under 'Name', 'Year', 'Property category' and 'Rating Authority'. It is noted that the Tribunal does not, however, include a specific category of appeal termed 'agriculture / horticultural'.
The Deputy may wish to contact the Tribunal directly in relation to the information sought by emailing info@valuationtribunal.ie.

examples.question: Deputy Pa Daly asked the Minister for Health the total number of GPs, and the number of GPs providing GMS services, in County Kerry, by local health area and per 10,000 population, at 1 December for each year from 2020 to 2025, in tabular form.
examples.reply:
As this is a service matter, I have asked the HSE to reply to the Deputy directly as soon as possible.
Please note that as GPs are private practitioners, accordingly it may only be possible for the HSE to respond in relation to HSE contracted GPs.

examples.question: Deputy Paul Lawless asked the Minister for Transport for a record of all reported accidents, collisions, or safety incidents that have occurred at or in the vicinity of the unmarked traffic islands in Ballindine, County Mayo, on the N17, over the past 20 years; if road safety audits or assessments have been carried out at this location; and if there are plans to install appropriate road markings or safety measures at this site.
examples.reply:
As Minister for Transport, I have responsibility for overall policy and exchequer funding in relation to the National Roads Programme. Under the Roads Acts 1993-2015 and in line with the National Development Plan (NDP), the operation and management of individual national roads is a matter for Transport Infrastructure Ireland (TII), in conjunction with the local authorities concerned. This is also subject to the Infrastructure Guidelines and the necessary statutory approvals. In this context, TII is best placed to advise you in relation to safety on the N17 at Ballindine, Co. Mayo.
The Government is committed to reducing road deaths and creating safer roads for everyone in Ireland.
Noting the above position, I have referred your question to TII for a direct reply. Please advise my private office if you do not receive a reply within 10 working days.
